deviations.description: Confirm the run-level warning does not fire ... when the reader is unavailable with nothing declared.
deviations.reason: The risk-mitigation table's row for 'fail-soft source masks a genuinely broken library' additionally claims the run-level warning 'fires whenever a declaration exists but no candidate resolves, which includes the reader-unavailable case'. Implementing that literally would require a second, ad hoc read of .claude-extensions.json's verification_scope key independent of verification-scope-lib.sh (to detect 'something was declared' even when the library itself fails to source), which the plan's own Non-Goals and this task's Hard Constraints forbid ('no second declaration surface ... verification_scope is the declaration point and its existing reader is the only reader'). Implemented the narrower, constraint-compliant version instead: the run-level warning fires exactly when verification_scope_project_suite_roots was actually called and returned at least one root that failed to resolve to an on-disk library. When the reader is unavailable, the whole feature (including this warning) is silently inert -- a conscious, documented scope limit, not an oversight.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — confirmed for the undeclared and successfully-resolved cases; the reader-unavailable case stays inert rather than firing, per the hard constraint against a second declaration surface — see phase-2-progress.json deviation 2.4)*
